title: AI Ad Examples: 25 AI-Generated Formats to Test
summary: AI ad examples in 25 formats for Facebook and Instagram, with real AI commercials, how they are made and Meta's AI labeling rules, checked October 2026.
body_markdown:
The most useful AI ad examples are formats you can repeat with your own product, not one-off visual tricks. An AI commercial is a video ad in which some or all of the footage, voice, presenter or animation was generated by AI models instead of filmed by a crew. This guide groups 25 AI-generated ad formats by the job each one does in Facebook and Instagram ads, points to real examples from Knowlify's client work and from well-known brands, and explains how these ads are made and labeled. If you want these formats made for you, Knowlify is the done-for-you agency we recommend.


**What these examples are.** Knowlify publishes this guide and makes AI video ads for Facebook and Instagram. The 25 formats are patterns to test, not performance claims, and we share no results for any ad mentioned here. Facts about other companies come from their own websites, checked October 26, 2026, and facts about Meta come from Meta's own pages.


## What is an AI commercial?


An AI commercial is an ad whose scenes, presenter, voice or edit were produced with generative AI rather than a camera. Runway, which sells AI video tools, describes one in its[guide to AI-generated commercials](https://runway.com/resources/ai-generated-commercials) as an ad where AI models, working from a prompt, an image or a brief, produce the footage, voice or edit that a camera crew would otherwise make (as of October 2026).


In practice, AI commercials sit on a spectrum:


- **Fully generated.** Every shot, voice and sound is generated, then edited together.
- **Hybrid.** Real product footage or screen recordings, with generated scenes, presenters or voiceover around them.
- **AI-assisted.** A filmed or designed ad that AI tools resize, extend or turn into more versions.


Meta builds some of this into Ads Manager itself. As of October 2026, its[Advantage+ creative page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/meta-advantage-plus/creative) says the tools use AI to generate and enhance ad variations across single image, video and carousel formats, and it names features including image expansion, background generation, video expansion and image animation. The same page says some enhancements may be on by default and can be turned off at any time. In a[January 2026 newsroom post](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/01/2026-ai-drives-performance/) , Meta reported that the combined revenue run-rate of its video generation tools reached $10 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025.


Those tools mostly vary an ad you already have. This guide is about the ad itself: the concept, script and footage.


## Which well-known AI commercials are worth studying?


Runway's guide points to three brand films and TV spots, described here only from each brand's own site (checked October 26, 2026). None of them is Knowlify's work.


Brand What was made AI tools or studios the brand names Where it ran


[Coca-Cola](https://www.coca-colacompany.com/media-center/coca-cola-refreshes-givers-of-the-season-embraces-ai-powered-storytelling-in-global-holiday-campaign) Two AI-driven reimaginations of its 1995 spot "The Holidays are Coming", a 60-second and a 90-second film, announced November 3, 2025 Studios Secret Level and Silverside AI; an executive refers to "GenAI tools" but no specific tool is named The release marks the 90-second film as airing only in the USA


[Kalshi](https://news.kalshi.com/p/week-ahead-nyc-elections-mideast-crisis-james-beard-awards) A fully AI-generated 30-second spot, made within days Google's Veo 3 Game 3 of the Oklahoma City vs. Indiana basketball championship series, per its June 16, 2025 newsletter


[Toys"R"Us](https://www.toysrus.com/pages/studios) A brand film imagining its founder, Charles Lazarus, and its mascot, Geoffrey the Giraffe, in the early 1930s OpenAI's Sora, with the partner Native Foreign Not stated on the page


Kalshi's own newsletter says its ad cost $2,000 to make. Coca-Cola's release says the music in its films was performed by real artists, and quotes a company executive saying creative direction stays human-led while AI helps with execution and production.


These pieces were made for a broad audience. A Facebook or Instagram ad has a different job: stop a scroll in Feed or Reels, make one point quickly and come in enough versions to test. The 25 formats below are built for that job.


## How are AI commercials made?


Most AI commercials follow roughly the same six steps, whichever tools are used. Runway's guide describes a similar sequence: concept and script, footage, audio, then edit and delivery.


Step What happens What a reviewer checks


1. Brief and script Audience, problem, one claim, the hook and a shot list Every claim is true and can be supported


2. Key frames A still image for each shot: the presenter, character, set or product Product shape, label and colors match the real product


3. Shot generation Each still becomes a short moving shot with an image-to-video or text-to-video model Hands, faces, text inside the frame and physical motion


4. Voice and sound Generated speech, a generated or recorded voiceover, music and sound effects Brand and product names are pronounced correctly, and the voice stays the same across shots


5. Edit Shots cut together with captions, cards, an end frame and one call to action The story still reads with the sound off, and there is only one ask


6. Versions and upload Exports for each placement, hook and length variants, upload to Ads Manager Vertical framing, key text in the safe zone and the right AI disclosure


The script and the review decide quality more than the choice of model. A video model can produce a product that does not exist, garbled lettering or a hand with the wrong number of fingers, and someone has to catch that before the ad ships. Meta's own[Ad Creative Generative AI Terms](https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/ad_creative_generative_ai_terms) make the advertiser solely responsible for checking the accuracy of output from Meta's tools (as of October 2026).


The finished ad usually runs vertically. As of October 2026, Meta's[Reels ads page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) recommends 9:16 video with audio and key messages kept inside the safe zone, clear of the Reels interface. It also says Reels play with sound on unless the viewer has turned sound off. Add captions anyway, so the story still reads in silence.


## Which AI ad examples work on Facebook and Instagram?


The 25 formats below are grouped by the kind of AI production they use. None is a guaranteed winner; each is a hypothesis to test against your own audience.


# Format What the viewer sees first Use it when


1 The specific problem A presenter naming one precise frustration The buyer already feels the problem


2 The routine The product inside a morning, workday or evening routine The setting explains why the product matters


3 The objection handler "I thought..." or a direct question, then visible proof One doubt blocks most purchases


4 The spokesperson explainer A presenter explaining what the category gets wrong The product needs a plain reason to exist


5 The comment reply A real customer question on screen, then the answer You have permission to show the question


6 The checklist talk A talking head with on-screen requirement cards A considered purchase has details the buyer must check


7 The twist-first story The surprising end of a story, then the backstory The product fits as one turning point in a personal story


8 The personified problem The problem as a character the viewer can see The pain is invisible or abstract


9 The animated metaphor A visual system for speed, security or focus The benefit is a concept, not an object


10 The exploded mechanism Parts or layers separating to show how it works The mechanism is hidden inside the product


11 The transformation A clear before state, then the after The product's role in the change can be shown


12 The skit Two people and one prop acting out a risk A technical risk needs a human face


13 The cinematic reveal Light, texture and camera motion on the product Premium positioning, with the product kept accurate


14 Mixed media Photos, type, interface and cutouts in motion You need visual change without new footage


15 The faceless voiceover Hands, product shots and B-roll under a voice A presenter would add nothing


16 The scene you cannot film A period, fantasy or impossible setting Filming the idea would cost more than the test is worth


17 Painful workflow to clean result The current multi-step process The product removes steps


18 One-feature proof A single action and its outcome One feature carries the purchase decision


19 Role-based use case The screen moments one role cares about Several roles buy the same product


20 Integration story A trigger, a connected tool and the automated result The value is in what the product connects


21 The FAQ ad One purchase-blocking question, answered Visitors stall on the same question


22 The demonstration reminder The product moment a visitor may have missed A demo explains more than the page did


23 The offer Price and conditions, readable and current A real offer exists, with no invented urgency


24 The short cutdown One hook, one proof and one ask A longer ad already works


25 The sequential story Part two of a story the viewer has already seen Each ad can answer the next question


### AI presenter formats (1 to 6)


These look like creator UGC, but the presenter is AI-generated, not a real customer or creator. Knowlify's 54-second ad for Parva, broken down in our[Facebook and Instagram video ad examples](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-video-ad-examples) , uses format 6: a presenter in scrubs talks to camera while two checklist cards hold the details a clinic owner would want to check.


Script them in the brand's voice, never as a fake customer. The FTC's[testimonials rule Q&A](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) says there is no blanket ban on AI-generated avatars in marketing, but an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false (as of October 2026). Our[AI UGC guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-ugc-ads) covers where the format fits and where it does not.


### 3D character and animation formats (7 to 11)


Parva's 27-second ad for patients uses format 7. It opens on the twist (she married her ex's brother), and the check-in app appears once, as the turning point of the story. Formats 8 to 11 suit value that is hard to film, such as a hidden mechanism. Our[3D animated video ads guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/3d-animated-video-ads) covers how these are produced.


### AI commercial formats (12 to 16)


Casco's 14-second ad uses format 12. An over-eager employee who booked a whole building when asked for a meeting room stands in for an AI agent with more access than it needs, and the single product line sits between two jokes. Format 16 is where the brand films above sit: AI makes an expensive scene affordable, but the product claim still has to be true. Our[AI commercial production guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-commercial-video-production) covers production and pricing.


### Demo and retargeting formats (17 to 25)


For software, use real screen recordings for the product and generate only the framing around it, such as a presenter, a metaphor or the before state. A generated interface that does not match the real product is a false demonstration. Retargeting formats work best as a series in which each ad answers the question the last one left open.
